 KALISPELL, Mont. — For some families, putting a meal on the table can be a challenge during the holiday season.
 On Friday, the Flathead Food Bank organized its holiday distribution, making sure hundreds of local families have a Thanksgiving meal to share. Organizers said demand for these distributions has been growing, highlighting the importance of community support during the holiday season.
 A line of cars was wrapped around the Flathead Food Bank, full of families looking to pick up their Thanksgiving meal.
 Even people who did not sign up ahead of time could still receive a holiday meal by visiting the food bank drive thru after 12 p.m. The food bank said it prepares extra meals to make sure it can serve everyone who comes in line.
 “We had roughly about 650 families signed up, but that family size could be three, four, five, six. We’re expecting to be able to serve thousands of folks throughout this distribution today," said Kelli Worley, major gifts officer at Flathead Food Bank. “They get a turkey here, they get a whole entire bag full of food, so really it's everything you could ever need for a Thanksgiving meal."
 Worley said the holiday season can be particularly difficult for families balancing everyday expenses with the cost of celebrating.
 “I think this time of year is definitely a harder time. I mean especially around the holidays, you’re wanting to focus on getting presents for your family too and have everyone come to town, so just being able to take the burden off the food need is just something that we’re really proud to be a part of," said Worley.
 Community support helps make distributions like this possible. The food bank said likely more than half of the food handed out came from donations.
 For the distribution, volunteers from Glacier Bank and WGM Group came out to hand out meals.
 Karen Benson has been volunteering with the food bank for fifteen years. She says it’s a reminder that anyone can find themselves in a position where they need a little extra help, especially around the holidays.
 “For people to know that they’re not alone, that there’s people that care and that there’s resources available for them gives hope to people during this season," said Benson, a volunteer from WGM Group.
 The Flathead Food Bank is planning another holiday distribution for Dec. 18, hoping to continue helping families through the holiday season.
